subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw trust and adopt these 14 new upstream action revisions in workflows that mint tokens, use secrets, publish artifacts, scan code, and run Codex agents?
rationale: The OpenClaw diff is mechanical, but approving new executable third-party revisions across privileged workflows is a repository trust decision that CI and automated review cannot make alone.

options.title: Approve after full verification
options.body: Verify the upstream revisions and direct Codex contract, refresh the branch, and merge after all affected exact-head checks complete successfully.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Separate token, release, registry, security-scanning, and Codex action bumps into narrower PRs if the combined trust review is too broad.

options.title: Keep current pins
options.body: Pause or close this batch if maintainers cannot confidently approve every privileged upstream revision.

recommendation.title: Approve after full verification
recommendation.body: Verify the upstream revisions and direct Codex contract, refresh the branch, and merge after all affected exact-head checks complete successfully.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-main history across the central CI and Codex-agent workflows touched by this batch.
